summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, end-stage renal disease with two kidney transplants, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and obstructive sleep apnea was admitted for acute decompensated heart failure due to volume overload, presenting with shortness of breath and leg swelling. He was treated with intravenous Lasix, successfully diuresed, and transitioned to oral torsemide 100mg daily. His tacrolimus dose was increased from 5mg to 7mg twice daily due to subtherapeutic levels, and he was advised to follow up for a tacrolimus level check. His weight stabilized at 181.7 pounds, and he was discharged home with instructions to monitor daily weight, adhere to medications, and follow up with cardiology and nephrology. A repeat sleep study for sleep apnea was recommended.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and with stage 5 chronic kidney disease, or end stage renal disease
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic peripheral angiopathy without gangrene
Acquired absence of left leg below knee
